title: Interception of registration/enrollment data in transit identifies the homeowner
description: Account-registration and device-enrollment traffic may contain direct identifiers (e.g., name, email, phone, account ID) or indirectly identifying device details tied to the household. If the flow is insufficiently protected in transit, an observer could identify the homeowner or household.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may traverse a network where an attacker can observe traffic and that registration payloads contain identifiers or unique device details.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Linkability via persistent identifiers and metadata on the enrollment flow
description: Persistent account identifiers, device serial numbers, MAC addresses, or stable network metadata in the registration/enrollment flow could allow an observer or intermediary to link multiple enrollment events to the same homeowner, household, or set of devices.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or metadata are present on the flow and visible to an observer or intermediary.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate; threat applicability depends on whether stable identifiers are exposed on this flow.

title: Excessive collection during account registration and device enrollment
description: The Home Hub may request or accept more personal data than necessary for account creation and device onboarding, such as unnecessary profile attributes, precise location, contact details, or detailed device metadata, creating a privacy threat through over-collection.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub design does not enforce data minimization for registration and onboarding.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory.

title: Secondary use of registration and device data beyond onboarding
description: Data provided for account registration and sensor/camera enrollment could later be used by the Home Hub for analytics, profiling, marketing, or other purposes not necessary for onboarding, exceeding the original purpose of collection.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub or its operators have access to retained registration/enrollment data and may repurpose it.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree label may vary.

title: Insufficient transparency about what data is collected during onboarding
description: The homeowner may not be adequately informed about which personal data and device attributes are collected during registration and enrollment, for what purposes, how long they are retained, and with whom they are shared.
assumptions: Assumes onboarding notices or UI disclosures may be incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory.

title: Invalid or non-granular consent for registration and device enrollment processing
description: The Home Hub may bundle necessary onboarding processing with optional uses, or fail to obtain valid, specific, and informed consent where consent is the legal basis, leading to non-compliant processing of homeowner and device data.
assumptions: Assumes some onboarding-related processing relies on consent or presents choices that are not sufficiently granular.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; legal basis may instead be contract for some processing.

title: Lack of evidence of homeowner choices during registration
description: If the Home Hub does not record the homeowner's registration actions, privacy notices shown, and choices made (e.g., consent or configuration selections), the homeowner may later be unable to prove what they agreed to or disputed, creating a non-repudiation-related privacy issue.
assumptions: Assumes auditability of privacy-relevant choices is weak or absent.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN's Non-repudiation category is less commonly applicable; included cautiously as a possible privacy issue.

title: Failure to support deletion of account or enrolled-device data
description: Registration and enrollment may create stored account records and device associations that cannot later be deleted or fully removed, undermining the homeowner's ability to have onboarding data erased when no longer needed.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub stores onboarding data and may lack deletion workflows or complete erasure mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact node naming may differ.

title: Interception of temporary access code in transit
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest may be observed or captured while being transmitted from the guest-facing input path to the Home Hub logic, allowing identification of the guest or association of the guest with a specific visit or property access event.
assumptions: Assumes the flow includes an electronically transmitted code entry path rather than a purely local mechanical action, and that an attacker can observe or tap the transmission channel.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identification via credential interception may differ.

title: Linkability of repeated guest access attempts
description: Metadata on this flow, such as timing, repeated code-entry attempts, or a stable temporary code value, could allow an observer to link multiple interactions to the same guest or the same guest stay, even if the guest's civil identity is not directly known.
assumptions: Assumes an observer can access flow metadata or repeated code submissions and that temporary codes are reused for a period of time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a generic linkability threat grounded in observable flow metadata and code reuse.

title: Disclosure of guest access code or access event at the Home Hub
description: Upon receipt, the Home Hub may store, display, or forward the temporary access code or associated access event details, disclosing that a guest accessed the front door at a particular time. This can reveal presence patterns and guest relationships.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub logs code entries, retains the code itself or event metadata, or shares events with other components or users.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may be more specific to stored credentials or event logs.

title: Unawareness of logging and secondary use of guest entry data
description: The guest may be unaware that entering the temporary access code causes the Home Hub to log the event, infer occupancy, or share the event with homeowners or service providers. This lack of transparency creates an unawareness threat.
assumptions: Assumes the guest is not clearly informed about logging, retention, recipients, or analytics performed on access events.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; exact unawareness subtree may distinguish lack of notice from lack of consent.

title: Processing guest access data beyond expected purpose or retention
description: The Home Hub may process or retain the temporary access code and related access timestamps longer than necessary, or use them for purposes beyond unlocking the door, such as profiling guest behavior or occupancy analytics, without a valid privacy basis.
assumptions: Assumes the system retains or repurposes code-entry data beyond immediate authentication.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id from memory; exact node may depend on the applicable compliance obligation (purpose limitation, data minimization, retention, or transparency).

title: Guest cannot plausibly deny having entered the property
description: If the Home Hub records successful code entry together with timestamps and code identifiers, the resulting evidence may prevent the guest from denying that they accessed the property at a specific time, which can create a privacy-relevant detectability/non-repudiation concern.
assumptions: Assumes logs are attributable to a specific temporary code assigned to one guest or booking.
uncertainty_note: Included because LINDDUN treats non-repudiation as a privacy threat; exact node id may be more specific to attributable audit logs.

title: Sensor event records can link activities over time to the same household or occupants
description: By writing motion, door, and other sensor events into a persistent local log, the Home Hub enables correlation of multiple events over time. This can link separate actions and routines to the same home, device set, or occupants, revealing behavioral patterns such as wake/sleep times, arrivals, departures, and room usage.
assumptions: The log stores timestamps and stable identifiers such as device IDs, room names, or household context, and entries persist long enough to be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Event contents may identify residents through unique behavior patterns
description: Even if the log does not explicitly name individuals, detailed sensor events combined with timestamps and device context can single out a resident or visitor through distinctive movement patterns, schedules, or interactions with specific doors and rooms.
assumptions: The home has a small number of occupants and the event granularity is sufficient to distinguish individuals indirectly.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat applicability depends on event granularity and household composition.

title: Local event log stores sensitive behavioral data that may be disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The destination data store accumulates intimate in-home activity data. If the log is accessed by unauthorized local users, malware, maintenance personnel, or other components without proper controls, it can disclose occupancy, routines, absences, and potentially security-relevant information.
assumptions: The data store is readable by some software or users beyond the minimum necessary, or lacks strong access control/encryption.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact disclosure subtree may differ.

title: Persistent logging enables inference of private habits and household state
description: The Local Event Log can be mined to derive information not explicitly recorded, such as when the home is empty, sleeping habits, religious practices, health-related routines, or relationships between occupants. These inferences arise from analysis of stored event sequences.
assumptions: Logs are retained over time and contain sufficiently frequent, timestamped sensor events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact detectability/disclosure distinction may vary by interpretation.

title: Residents may be unaware of the extent and persistence of local event logging
description: If the Local Event Log stores detailed sensor events without clear notice, residents and visitors may not understand that their movements and interactions are being continuously recorded and retained locally. This undermines their ability to make informed privacy decisions.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate logging behavior, retention, or access to the log.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a transparency/unawareness threat centered on the destination's logging behavior.

title: Logging may exceed user expectations or stated purpose for home automation
description: Storing detailed motion and door events in a persistent local log may be unnecessary or excessive relative to the immediate automation purpose, especially if retained longer than needed or reused for diagnostics, profiling, or secondary purposes without a valid basis or user control.
assumptions: Retention is longer than operationally necessary, or the data is reused beyond core automation functions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact non-compliance subtree may differ depending on the compliance framework in scope.

title: Uploading clips reveals occupants' activities to the cloud provider
description: By sending recorded camera clips from the Home Hub to cloud storage, the source discloses highly sensitive in-home video content that can reveal occupants, visitors, routines, possessions, and behavior patterns to the receiving service.
assumptions: Recorded clips contain identifiable people or household context and are accessible to the cloud service in intelligible form.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure by sharing content; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Upload metadata can link clips to a specific household or account
description: Even if clip contents are protected, flow metadata such as device identifiers, account identifiers, IP address, timing, clip frequency, and destination bucket/object naming can allow the uploads to be linked to the same home, user account, or device over time.
assumptions: Transport or surrounding service logs expose stable identifiers or observable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via communication metadata.

title: Transmission metadata can identify the household or residents
description: Identifiers and network metadata carried with or alongside the upload, such as account IDs, device serial numbers, IP address, or precise timestamps, may enable identification of the household or inference of who lives there.
assumptions: The cloud service or intermediaries can observe these identifiers or correlate them with subscriber records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from data-flow metadata; exact subtree may differ.

title: Traffic patterns disclose occupancy and behavior
description: The timing, size, and frequency of clip uploads can reveal when motion occurred, when residents are home or away, sleep/work routines, and unusual events, even without viewing the video content itself.
assumptions: An observer at the cloud side or on the network can access upload timing and volume metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure through side-channel/metadata rather than payload.

title: Stored clips can be linked across time to build household behavior profiles
description: At the destination, cloud video storage can aggregate uploaded clips over long periods and link them to the same account, device, address, or household, enabling longitudinal profiling of routines, visitors, and events.
assumptions: The datastore retains stable account/device identifiers and historical uploads.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability caused by recipient-side aggregation.

title: Cloud storage can identify individuals appearing in clips
description: Once received, the cloud service may identify residents, visitors, or neighbors from the video itself or by combining clips with account records, facial recognition, voice, location, or billing data.
assumptions: The service has access to clip contents and auxiliary subscriber data or analytics capabilities.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for recipient-side identifiability through content and correlation.

title: Cloud retention and internal access disclose intimate in-home footage
description: The destination may store clips for extended periods or make them accessible to administrators, contractors, analytics systems, or third parties, increasing the chance that intimate household footage is exposed beyond what users expect.
assumptions: Cloud storage is not strictly end-to-end encrypted against the provider and retention/access controls may exceed user expectations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure due to storage, access, or onward use at the recipient.

title: Secondary use of uploaded clips may exceed the original home-security purpose
description: The cloud provider may use stored clips for analytics, model training, service improvement, law-enforcement response workflows, or sharing with affiliates, which may be incompatible with the user's original expectation of simple backup/storage for home security.
assumptions: Terms or backend practices permit secondary processing beyond necessary storage and retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for policy/expectation mismatch and secondary use.

title: Users may lack awareness or control over cloud retention and sharing of clips
description: Individuals recorded by the cameras, and even the account holder, may not have meaningful notice, consent options, or granular control over how long clips are retained in cloud storage, who can access them, or whether they are shared onward.
assumptions: The service provides limited transparency or coarse privacy controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/lack of consent or insufficient transparency; exact subtree may vary.

title: The cloud provider may be able to deny specific accesses or disclosures without sufficient auditability
description: If access to stored clips and onward disclosures are not strongly logged and attributable, the destination or its operators may later deny having viewed, shared, or exported particular recordings, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Audit logs are incomplete, mutable, or not exposed for verification.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability in LINDDUN can be context-dependent; node id is a best estimate.

title: Excessive disclosure of occupancy information by forwarding motion alerts
description: By forwarding a real-time motion alert, the Home Hub discloses that motion was detected at a specific home and time. This can reveal presence/occupancy patterns of residents beyond what may be strictly necessary for backend processing.
assumptions: The alert contains or is associated with household/device identifiers and a timestamp, and backend processing could have been designed with less granular data in some cases.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for a disclosure-by-sharing threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability of repeated motion alerts on the flow
description: Repeated motion alerts sent from the same Home Hub to the backend can be linked together via persistent device, account, network, or protocol identifiers, enabling construction of behavioral patterns for a household over time.
assumptions: The flow uses stable identifiers or otherwise exposes metadata that allows correlating multiple alerts to the same home/account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via message metadata/correlation; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Identifiability of the household from alert metadata
description: Even if the alert payload is minimized, metadata on the flow such as device identifiers, account references, IP address, or routing information may allow the backend or intermediaries to identify the specific household generating the motion alert.
assumptions: The communication exposes stable identifiers or network metadata observable by recipients or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from data/metadata in transit; exact numbering may vary.

title: Backend stores or further disseminates detailed motion events
description: Upon receipt, the mobile app backend may retain, analyze, or share detailed motion-event records with other services, operators, or third parties, disclosing sensitive in-home activity information beyond the immediate alerting purpose.
assumptions: The backend persists event logs or forwards them to analytics, support, or partner systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure caused by recipient-side storage/use/sharing; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Use of motion alerts for secondary purposes without user expectation
description: The backend could use received motion alerts for profiling, product analytics, model training, or marketing-related inferences that are not expected by residents when the alert is generated.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and consent controls are absent or insufficiently enforced at the backend.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unintended secondary use; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for backend processing of motion alerts
description: Residents may not be adequately informed, or may not have meaningfully consented, to the backend receiving and processing real-time motion alerts and deriving occupancy insights from them.
assumptions: Notice/consent mechanisms do not clearly explain this data transfer and its implications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/consent regarding collection and processing; exact numbering may vary.

title: Lack of evidence about backend handling of motion alerts
description: If the backend does not maintain adequate, privacy-respecting audit records, it may be impossible for users or operators to later prove whether a motion alert was received, accessed, shared, or deleted, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Auditability and user-visible processing records are limited or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation/accountability gaps; exact numbering may vary.

title: Notification content discloses occupancy or in-home activity
description: By pushing a motion-detected notification to the homeowner, the backend may disclose sensitive facts such as that someone is currently moving inside or near the home, implying occupancy patterns, routines, or security events. If the notification text is detailed, the disclosure is caused by the backend's choice of content to share.
assumptions: Assumes the push notification contains explicit motion-event details rather than a generic alert.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary depending on whether the taxonomy distinguishes content disclosure by data sharing versus storage.

title: Push-notification metadata can link homeowner and household events
description: Even if notification payloads are encrypted or minimized, metadata on the flow—such as device token, timing, frequency, and association with a specific backend account—can allow linking repeated motion events to the same homeowner or household over time.
assumptions: Assumes push delivery involves stable identifiers or observable timing metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability via communication metadata.

title: Notification delivery metadata can identify the homeowner or household
description: Identifiers used to route the push notification, such as device tokens, account identifiers, or correlated network/provider metadata, may enable identification of the homeowner or their residence from this flow.
assumptions: Assumes routing uses persistent identifiers and that some party on the path or supporting infrastructure can associate them with a person or address.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ if LINDDUN Pro separates direct identifiers from indirect identification through metadata.

title: Notification preview on the device or lock screen discloses event details in transit to the user context
description: The flow may result in sensitive motion-event details being exposed through notification previews before the homeowner intentionally opens the app, allowing bystanders near the phone to learn about activity at the home.
assumptions: Assumes notification content is shown on lock screen or wearable previews by default.
uncertainty_note: Positioned on the flow because the disclosure stems from how the notification is transmitted and presented en route to the recipient; some analysts might instead place this at the destination context.

title: Recipient-side retention or onward sharing of notifications discloses household activity
description: Once received, the homeowner's device or user context may retain notifications in notification history, backups, synced wearables, or screenshots, causing further disclosure of motion events and occupancy patterns beyond the immediate alert.
assumptions: Assumes the phone ecosystem stores or syncs notifications, or the user may share them onward.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure caused at the destination after receipt.

title: Homeowner may be unaware of detailed motion-event notifications being pushed
description: If the backend sends detailed motion notifications by default, the homeowner may not fully understand that sensitive in-home activity summaries are being proactively pushed to the phone and potentially exposed outside the app.
assumptions: Assumes defaults or UX do not clearly explain notification granularity and exposure risks.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping for unawareness about notification behavior may differ.

title: Insufficient choice or consent over notification content and timing
description: If the backend sends motion-detected notifications without granular controls or valid consent for detailed alerts, the homeowner may lack meaningful control over whether sensitive household activity is pushed to their device.
assumptions: Assumes notification preferences are absent, coarse, or pre-enabled.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance/consent-control issues; exact taxonomy branch may vary.

title: Shared aggregated analytics may still enable linkage across sessions or cohorts
description: Even if the backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics, the chosen aggregation dimensions, timestamps, app version, region, device model, or cohort identifiers may allow the vendor to link records belonging to the same user, household, or small group across reporting periods.
assumptions: Assumes the aggregation is not sufficiently coarse and that repeated submissions contain stable quasi-identifiers or cohort keys.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability from disclosure/sharing; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Aggregated analytics may still permit inference of individual or small-group identity
description: If aggregates are computed over small populations or rare combinations of attributes, the vendor may be able to single out or infer the identity of a user or a very small group from the shared analytics.
assumptions: Assumes low-count buckets, rare device/app combinations, or auxiliary data available to the vendor.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability via insufficient aggregation/k-anonymity; exact node id may differ.

title: Sharing usage analytics discloses behavioral information beyond user expectations
description: Device-usage analytics can reveal behavioral patterns such as feature adoption, frequency of use, time-of-day habits, or engagement trends. Even in aggregated form, this may disclose sensitive information about user populations or niche cohorts to the vendor.
assumptions: Assumes analytics include meaningful behavioral dimensions and that some cohorts may be sensitive or small.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ depending on whether emphasis is on content or derived knowledge.

title: Vendor may use received analytics for secondary purposes
description: Upon receipt, the cloud analytics vendor may retain, profile, combine, or repurpose the aggregated analytics for its own product improvement, benchmarking, model training, or commercial analytics beyond the original purpose of supporting this mobile app.
assumptions: Assumes contractual or technical controls do not fully prevent secondary use.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for disclosure/processing at destination; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Vendor can correlate received analytics with other customer or platform data
description: The vendor may combine this app's aggregated analytics with telemetry from other clients, SDK data, account metadata, or market datasets to link cohorts, organizations, or recurring populations across datasets.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor operates at scale and has access to auxiliary datasets enabling cross-dataset correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by destination-side correlation; exact node id may differ.

title: Vendor may re-identify individuals or small cohorts using auxiliary data
description: Although the backend sends aggregated analytics, the vendor may combine them with other information it holds to infer the identity of individuals, devices, or narrowly defined cohorts represented in the aggregates.
assumptions: Assumes access to auxiliary datasets and sufficiently granular aggregates.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node for destination-side re-identification; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that analytics are shared with an external vendor
description: If the app's notices do not clearly explain that aggregated device-usage analytics are sent to a third-party cloud analytics vendor, users may lack awareness of the collection, sharing, recipients, and purposes of processing.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or in-app disclosures are incomplete, unclear, or hard to access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness regarding third-party sharing; exact node id may differ.

title: Sharing may exceed consent or stated purpose limitations
description: The backend's transfer of analytics to the vendor may be incompatible with the consent obtained from users, the stated privacy notice, or internal purpose-limitation and data-minimization commitments, especially if users did not agree to third-party analytics sharing.
assumptions: Assumes consent, legitimate-interest balancing, or notice coverage is absent, ambiguous, or narrower than the actual sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Vendor retention and onward use may violate contractual or regulatory constraints
description: The vendor's storage duration, onward transfers, cross-border processing, or reuse of the analytics may fail to comply with applicable privacy obligations or agreed processing terms.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient data-processing agreement controls, retention limits, or transfer safeguards.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for destination-side processing; exact node id may differ.

title: Linkability via repeated video-retrieval metadata
description: Metadata on this retrieval flow (e.g., clip identifier, camera/device identifier, homeowner account identifier, timestamps, IP/session information, and frequency of access) could allow an observer or intermediary with access to network or application telemetry to link multiple playback requests to the same household, camera, or user over time.
assumptions: Assumes retrieval requests/responses generate observable metadata in transit or in logs associated with the flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability from communication metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Identifiability of homeowner or household from flow metadata
description: Even if the video payload is protected, identifiers and contextual metadata carried with the request/response or exposed by transport/logging could identify the homeowner, household, or specific camera location to parties observing the flow.
assumptions: Assumes account IDs, device IDs, URLs/object keys, or network metadata are present or inferable during transfer.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability through data-flow metadata.

title: Disclosure of sensitive video content in transit
description: The retrieved clip may contain highly sensitive personal data (occupants, visitors, routines, interiors, audio, timestamps). If the transfer is intercepted, insufficiently encrypted, exposed through debugging/proxy infrastructure, or broadly logged, the video content could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the clip or derived content traverses infrastructure where interception, misconfiguration, or excessive logging is possible.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for disclosure of data in transit/content exposure.

title: Over-disclosure by cloud storage when serving the clip
description: Cloud Video Storage may return more data than necessary for playback, such as extra metadata, adjacent clips, thumbnails, audio tracks, retention metadata, or internal object identifiers, thereby disclosing additional personal information beyond what the backend needs for the requested playback.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 can package or expose ancillary metadata/content together with the requested clip.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for source-side excessive disclosure; exact subnode may differ.

title: Disclosure through backend logging, caching, or onward sharing
description: Upon receiving the clip, the Mobile App Backend may cache, log, replicate, transcode, or forward the video and its metadata in ways that expose it to administrators, analytics systems, support tooling, or other internal services not necessary for homeowner playback.
assumptions: Assumes P2 performs storage, logging, monitoring, debugging, or integration with other services after receipt.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side disclosure after receipt.

title: Secondary use of retrieved video beyond homeowner playback
description: The backend could use the retrieved clip or associated metadata for purposes beyond the stated playback function, such as analytics, model training, employee review, product improvement, or law-enforcement response preparation, without the data subject's expectation or valid basis.
assumptions: Assumes governance or technical controls do not strictly limit P2 to playback-only processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for unauthorized/secondary use at the destination.

title: Non-compliance with data minimization and purpose limitation during retrieval
description: If P2 retrieves full-resolution clips, unnecessary time ranges, or excessive metadata when only a limited segment is needed for playback, the processing may violate privacy requirements such as data minimization, storage limitation, or purpose limitation.
assumptions: Assumes the system could technically request narrower or less detailed data than it currently retrieves.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for compliance-related over-collection/over-processing.

title: Insufficient evidence of accountable retrieval
description: If the backend does not maintain reliable audit records of which user requested which clip and why, it may be difficult to prove or dispute whether a particular video retrieval was legitimate, undermining accountability for privacy-sensitive access.
assumptions: Assumes auditability of playback access is required for dispute handling or compliance.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow; included as an accountability/privacy concern with approximate node id.
